items.title: How Raúl Castro’s Grandson, Raúl G. Rodríguez Castro, Became a Power Broker
items.summary: The Castro family envoy, Raúl G. Rodríguez Castro, who has been in talks with the Trump administration, was once named in a case targeting a Cuban smuggling ring.

items.title: Russian Civilian Deaths Are Growing Rapidly as Ukraine Expands Its Air War
items.summary: The higher tempo of Ukrainian strikes has fueled discontent among Russians, but it is far from clear that it will change the Kremlin’s calculus about the war.

items.title: A Syrian Holdout Province, Sweida, Fears a Government Takeover
items.summary: In Sweida Province, dominated by the country’s Druse minority, many say it is just a matter of time before the central government moves to assert control over the region.

items.title: The Eclipse Is Coming, and Iceland Is Looking for a Break in the Clouds
items.summary: Rooms were booked years ago, and officials have been making plans. But there’s no telling where, exactly, Icelanders might go to find the best possible view.

items.title: As Death Toll From Colombia Earthquake Rises to at Least 181, Rescuers Hunt for Survivors
items.summary: “We heard them screaming,” said one rescuer in Cali, where emergency workers and volunteers are racing against time to find the living trapped in the rubble.

items.title: Four Killed in Houthi Strike on Red Sea Ship, Yemeni Government Says
items.summary: The Yemeni government said the ship was carrying food supplies to a port on the Bab al-Mandab Strait while the Iran-backed Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of transporting weapons.

items.title: Ex-Marine Robert Gilman Is Freed by Russia After 4 Years in Prison
items.summary: The Kremlin released Robert Gilman, whose family and an advocacy group had said he was in dire physical condition, on “a humanitarian basis,” President Trump said.

items.title: Why Rumors About Morocco Followed Spain’s Ceuta Migrant Surge
items.summary: Claims swirled that Morocco, perhaps spurred by Israel and the United States, organized a recent border disaster. That unproven speculation, experts said, was exacerbated by the region’s complicated history.

items.title: Syria Sentences Former President al-Assad to Death for Crimes Against Humanity
items.summary: The former president was convicted of crimes against humanity during the country’s civil war, the first verdict since he fled to Russia in 2024.

items.title: What We Know About the Earthquake in Colombia
items.summary: The 7.4-magnitude quake, which killed more than 100 people and damaged hundreds of buildings, was the strongest recorded in Colombia in a decade.

items.title: David Ellison Floats Hollywood Exit as States Threaten His Warner Bros. Deal
items.summary: Mr. Ellison told Paramount executives that he was considering pulling the company out of California amid a lawsuit brought by state attorneys general.

items.title: Judge Awards $250,000 to Musician Who Fled Trump-Led Kennedy Center Gig
items.summary: The center had sued Chuck Redd when he canceled a free concert last year, citing the addition of the Trump name to the venue. But a judge dismissed the case.

items.title: Frenzy for Solar Eclipse Glasses Takes Over London
items.summary: Ahead of Wednesday’s rare cosmic event, thousands of people in London are searching for protective eyewear, as prices surge and stocks sell out.

items.title: G.M.’s ‘Car Guy’ Talks Electrics, China and Nepotism
items.summary: Mark Reuss became the automaker’s president seven years ago, ascending to a role his father was fired from decades before. We got the chance to speak with him.

items.title: Robots That Walk and Talk Are Coming to Car Factories
items.summary: But experts warn they may not deliver the gains in efficiency that proponents claim.

items.title: Ari Emanuel’s Company to Acquire 7 Broadway Theaters and 10 in the West End
items.summary: The purchase of ATG Entertainment, which operates dozens of venues worldwide, will require regulatory approval.

items.title: The Perils of Wall St.’s Race to Pour Billions More Into A.I.
items.summary: Investors including BlackRock have committed an eye-popping amount to lend to the artificial intelligence industry. That enthusiasm isn’t shared by everyone.

items.title: Oil Prices Touch $90 a Barrel Over U.S.-Iran Stalemate
items.summary: The stalemate over the Iran war hardened and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continued to dwindle.

items.title: Heat, Fire, Smoke and Storms Are Wreaking Havoc on the Economy
items.summary: Businesses are reckoning with the financial toll of this year’s brutal climate shocks.

items.title: How Social Media Sparked a Refugee Crisis Between Spain and Morocco
items.summary: A wave of disinformation online contributed to a surge of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta who were trying to reach Europe, resulting in about 90 deaths.

items.title: His Start-Up’s Goal: A.I. That Is Trainable and Not Controlled by a Big Company
items.summary: A co-founder of xAI is going all in on building open-source artificial intelligence so that “anyone can control and shape A.I. for their own needs.”

items.title: Wall St. Wants Another Half-Trillion Dollars for the A.I. Boom
items.summary: Six giant investment firms announced a $500 billion effort to raise money for customers of Nvidia to pay for computing power.

items.title: Waymo Is Growing Faster Than Ever. So Are Its ‘Edge Cases.’
items.summary: As Waymo deploys more driverless cars to 15 U.S. cities and counting, its vehicles keep encountering new and unexpected situations that they have no script to handle.

items.title: Spotify Will Label A.I. Artists and Avoid Promoting Them
items.summary: The new label, which will begin to be applied next month, is an effort by the streaming service to be more transparent about A.I.-generated music on its app.

items.title: Brad Lightcap, a Top OpenAI Executive, Steps Down
items.summary: Brad Lightcap, a longtime leader, said he was starting a new venture. His exit from the artificial intelligence company is the latest in a series there.

items.title: Meta Unveils an Open Version of Its Most Powerful A.I. Model
items.summary: The release of Muse Glimmer, a model that can be freely downloaded and modified, is likely to intensify a debate over whether A.I. should be restricted.

items.title: A.I.-Driven Chip Crunch Leads to New Rush of Lobbying in Washington
items.summary: As data centers gobble up memory chips, other industries that need the components, including electronics companies like Apple and medical device makers, are asking for government help.

items.title: Can A.I. Get You Where You Want to Go for Less?
items.summary: A wave of new services uses A.I. to monitor flights and hotel reservations to help you find lower prices. We look at how these tools work.

items.title: Flock Cameras Are Dividing U.S. Cities. Here’s What to Know About Them.
items.summary: Flock Safety’s automated license plate-reading cameras, used by thousands of law enforcement agencies in the U.S., have drawn intense criticism from civil liberties groups.
